Chapter 10: The Ongoing Work of Becoming
You know, it's easy to imagine that one day, everything in life will just... settle down. That all our big questions will finally get answered, the tough parts will smooth out, and the family will feel complete. But for these partners, life doesn’t really work that way. It’s this ongoing process—always shifting, always becoming something new. There’s always another challenge, another joy, another way to grow together.
As their child gets older, new questions keep popping up. Like, how do you talk about what makes us different in a way that feels empowering, not shameful? Or, how do you truly support each other through all the changes—through the grief, and even those everyday disappointments that sneak up on us? And maybe the biggest one: how do you keep loving, keep hoping, keep building something beautiful, even when the world seems set on holding you back?
There aren’t any simple answers here. Some days, these partners feel strong—like they can take on anything together. Other days? They’re tired. Maybe a little uncertain, maybe even afraid. But no matter what, they keep showing up. For themselves, for each other, for their child. That’s where they discover something powerful: becoming isn’t really about reaching a destination. It’s a way of living. It’s about staying open, being willing to keep trying, and—most of all—choosing to keep loving.
When the partners look back on everything—the risks they took, the losses they faced, the moments that made their hearts soar—they can see how far they’ve come. How much they’ve truly grown. And sure, the work isn’t ever really finished. There will always be another challenge, another possibility waiting ahead. But here’s the thing—they know they’re not alone. There are others out there, too, building their lives from the edges, standing up for the right to exist, to love, to become.
